title: DialogWright slots.yaml
description: The app's slots by id, in the order they are filled and acknowledged. Lists every slot the app has: a library type with its options, or { type: code } for a slot the code writes.

keypad.description: Whether the caller can key the date on the keypad as eight digits, month, day and year (MMDDYYYY), or in a day-first locale (Spanish) day, month and year (DDMMYYYY). Needs an ask_<slot>_dtmf line.

readNumbers.description: Whether a date of birth said only in numbers, at the slot's own question, is read from its digits the way the keypad reads them ("oh eight two one nineteen eighty four", "eight twenty one eighty four", "08/21/1984"), in place of the model's month and day: a run the digits read one way only, a real day from `minYear` to yesterday, is the value (or a month and day alone, the partial) once the model judges a birth date is stated; any other run of numbers is not read (see `numbersExample`). A turn with a word that is not a number (a month name, "the", "first") or a year alone is the model's, as before. false: the model reads every turn.

numbersExample.description: Whether a date said only in numbers that gives no date (a run the digits cannot read one way, or, with `readNumbers: false`, one the model hears no date in) is asked again with an example of a date said in a way that is understood: the outcome is invalid, reason numbers_unclear, and the re-ask is ask_<slot>_example, which the app words (and, with `keypad`, may offer the keypad in). false: the slot's generic retry asks again. Needs an ask_<slot>_example line.

yearPrompt.description: The prompt that asks for the year alone once a month and day are heard without it (the slot's partialPromptId). Default: ask_<slot>_year.

wholePrompt.description: The prompt that asks for the whole date again when a month or a day was not heard; the outcome is invalid, with the reason no_month_day, no_month or no_day. Absent: the outcome is invalid with the reason no_year and the slot's generic retry asks again.

minYear.description: The earliest year a date of birth may be in. An earlier one is invalid (reason impossible), and the keypad refuses it.

notThisDate.description: Another date the caller is likely to mention, which the birth date is not, as a noun phrase ("an appointment date", "the date of the order"). The default month and day questions then say "This is the birth date, not <it>.", and the default "false" criterion names it.

redact.description: How the value is masked wherever it leaves the turn (the trace, the console, a tool call's param of the same name): "mask" keeps the year only ("••/••/1985"); "none" keeps it as it is.

handoff.description: What a transfer to a person hands over: the date as it is said ("display"), or, for a birth date asked to verify identity, only whether the caller was "verified". app.yaml's handoff.data then says whether it goes, and how: by default an identity factor is left out and a redacted value masked.

confirm.description: "summary": a birth date is neither acknowledged nor read back on its own; the form's final confirm covers it. "always": the birth date is read back for a yes as soon as it is heard (confirm_<slot>, given its display as {<slot>}), before the form goes on; a no empties the slot and asks it again (ack_declined, then ask_<slot>, or ask_<slot>_dtmf at the keypad rung where the slot takes keys), a step on its ladder, and a second no goes to a person. The right answer said with the no ("no, it's ...") is taken.

text.description: Text to say to the model in place of a default, word for word, by part: given, givenTrue, givenFalse, month, monthHint, day, dayHint, year, yearAsked, yearNone.

given.description: The yes-or-no question that asks whether the caller states their date of birth at all.

givenTrue.description: What a yes to the first question means (its "true" criterion).

givenFalse.description: What a no to the first question means (its "false" criterion). By default it names `notThisDate`, when given, and someone else's birth date.

month.description: The question that asks which month the birth date is in. Its choices are the twelve months and none. By default it ends with the `notThisDate` sentence and `monthHint`.

monthHint.description: A sentence the default month question ends with, such as how a month said as a number is read. Default: none.

day.description: The question that asks which day of the month the birth date is. Its choices are 1 to 31 and none. By default it ends with the `notThisDate` sentence and `dayHint`.

dayHint.description: A sentence the default day question ends with, such as which number of a date said as numbers is the day. Default: none.

year.description: The question that asks which span of the caller's words is the year, when no month and day are on hand. Its choices are the spans the engine finds, and none.

yearAsked.description: The year question in place of `year` while a month and day are on hand, so the caller was just asked for the year alone (they may still restate the whole date).

yearNone.description: What the year question's "none" choice means.

ids.description: Question ids in place of the defaults (the slot's id followed by the part: given, month, day, year), to keep the ids an existing slot used.

given.description: The id of the question that asks whether the caller states their date of birth.

month.description: The id of the question that asks which month the date of birth is in.

day.description: The id of the question that asks which day of the month the date of birth is.

year.description: The id of the question that asks which span of the caller's words is the year of birth.

listen.description: Where the slot listens outside a form. "up-front": asked there, and a value kept only when the turn enters a form that has the slot (values said up front with the request). "form": asked and filled only while a form that has it is open; outside one its question is not sent. "anywhere": a value said outside a form is kept when said on a turn that opens no form, or with the request for a form that has the slot, until a form that has the slot uses it; a turn that opens a form without it keeps nothing for it. "call": as anywhere, and kept for the whole call, across forms (what app.yaml's carrySlots does). An identity factor listens as identity.yaml says, and takes none. Without it, the slot listens as its forms say (forms.yaml listenBeforeEntered): "form" when every form that lists it says false (the default for an internal form), else "up-front".

offer.description: Propose a value in place of the question. "facts": when the form would ask the slot and the app's facts have a value for it (code.facts.offers; e.g. the street the call-start lookup found for the number calling, or one a form's entry call loaded after identity), the line asks offer_<slot> as a yes or no, with the value as {<slot>} ("Is this about 22 Alder Street?"), once per slot per form. A yes fills the slot with it, confirmed, and nothing else: never who the caller is or their identity level. A no asks ask_<slot> with no attempt counted, and a value said instead fills as said. Needs code.facts.offers, and offer_<slot> in every locale. Never on an identity factor, nor beside callerNumber, nor on a slot redacted by its length (its words are never said back).

offerAt.description: Where a slot with offer: facts proposes. "slot" (the default): when its form would ask it. "greeting": at call start, on a call, after the call-start lookup, in place of the greeting's open question (greeting_offer, then offer_<slot>), when the facts have a value for it then; otherwise at the slot. One greeting proposal per call, the first such slot in slots.yaml order. A yes fills the slot, confirmed, kept for whichever form uses it, and greet_after_offer asks the open question; a yes with a request goes on to the request. A no, or a request with neither, leaves the slot to be asked in its form, not proposed again there. Needs offer: facts, and greeting_offer and greet_after_offer in every locale.

offerAnswers.description: What a slot with offer: facts takes at its proposal. "yes-no-or-value" (the default): a yes, a no, or a value of the caller's own, which fills the slot as said. "yes-no": a yes or a no only. A value said at the proposal is not taken, and with no clear yes it is a no (the slot's question is then asked); on the keypad 1 is yes and 2 is no. Use yes-no where the line asks only a yes or no question ("Are you calling about the account ending in 1234?"). Needs offer: facts.

askedOf.description: The callers the slot is asked of: principal kinds as identity.yaml names them (the subject kind, or a delegate kind such as broker), or a delegate kind and one of its roles (broker.office_admin). For any other caller the slot is not part of its forms: its question is not sent, it is not asked, and its form completes without it (a caller not yet verified is no kind listed but anonymous, which may not be listed). Use it for what only some callers need to say, such as which client a delegate is asking about. Never on an identity factor; pnpm check refuses a kind or a role identity.yaml does not have. Default: every caller.

attempts.description: How many failed answers the slot takes before onMaxAttempts, 1 to 10. Each failure before the last but one re-asks: a missed answer with ask_<slot>_retry, or ask_<slot>_retry2 at the second failure (and so on) where prompts.yaml has it; a silence with ask_<slot>_noinput2 (and so on), else ask_<slot>_noinput, else no_input then the question (ask_<slot>) again (at the keypad rung of a slot that takes no keys, on a channel with a keypad, no_input then its retry line). The last but one is the keypad rung (ask_<slot>_dtmf) where the slot takes keys and the channel has a keypad, else another re-ask; the last runs onMaxAttempts. Default: the engine's MAX_ATTEMPTS (3).

say.description: The line said (a prompt in prompts.yaml); it renders with the form's slot displays as variables, as the summary does. Required for end and anything-else; for the others, said first.

then.description: What follows the line: end (the call ends after the line; with a request queued, the call goes on to it); anything-else (the form closes uncompleted and the call carries on: the next queued request, or "anything else?"); handoff (to a person, with the handoff line handoff_<reason>); form (the form closes uncompleted and the form named by `form` is entered, as a next: is, keeping the slots both list); skip (the slot is left empty and declined, and the form goes on to its next question).

reason.description: For then: handoff, the handoff reason, whose line is handoff_<reason>. Default: max-attempts.

form.description: For then: form, the form entered: a form in forms.yaml (an internal one too).

goodbye.description: For then: end, whether the app's goodbye line follows `say`. false: the call ends on `say` alone, for a line that says goodbye itself ("... We're closed right now. Goodbye."), so the caller does not hear goodbye twice. Default true: the goodbye follows the line. Either way, with a request queued the line is said and the call goes on to it, so a line that may be followed by one keeps the goodbye out of its words (only a start route never has one).

onMaxAttempts.description: What happens when the slot runs out of attempts (a missed answer, a silence, an unanswered read-back, or a second no to its read-back). "handoff" (the default): to a person, with handoff_max_attempts. "skip": the slot is left empty and declined, and the form goes on; never on an identity factor, nor on a slot its form's summary names. Or written out, { say, then, reason, form, goodbye }: then is handoff (reason names the handoff, default max-attempts), skip, end (say required; the call ends, the goodbye after the line unless goodbye: false), anything-else (say required; the form closes uncompleted and "anything else?" is asked) or form (the form closes uncompleted and `form` is entered, keeping the slots both list); say, a prompt said first. An offer of the caller's number with onNo: skip that runs out leaves the slot empty whatever this says; with no onNo: skip, the slot's ladder goes on to it.

oneOf.description: A caller's date of birth: a month, a day and a year, heard whole or in part.

options.description: The options the caller can choose, in order, as `key: Say` or `key: { say, means }`, at most 200. The key is the value the slot takes and the label the model chooses; `say` is how it is said; the order is the order of the keypad (1, 2, 3, ...) and of the labels the model is offered.

say.description: The display: how a line, the summary and the model's turn state say the option ("an express delivery").

means.description: What the model is told this option is: the text of its criterion, sent exactly as written. Default: the slot's `means` template.
The criterion the model is given for each option that has no `means` of its own, as a template over `{say}` and `{key}`.

text.description: Text to say to the model in place of a default, word for word, by part: instructions, none.

instructions.description: The question that asks which option the caller names, sent to the model in place of the default.

none.description: What the question's "none" label means: the caller names no option.

keypad.description: Whether the caller can key the option, by its position (1 for the first), after spoken answers missed. At most 9 options. Needs an ask_<slot>_dtmf line.

fillAt.description: The threshold the model's probability for the option must reach for the slot to fill; below it the slot stays empty.

confirm.description: "summary": a chosen option is neither acknowledged nor read back on its own; the form's final confirm covers it. "by-confidence": it is acknowledged (ack_<slot>, given the option's display as {<slot>}) when `readBack` says so, and always when the caller hedged (`hedge`). "always": a chosen option is read back for a yes as soon as it is heard (confirm_<slot>, given its display as {<slot>}), before the form goes on; a no empties the slot and asks it again (ack_declined, then ask_<slot>, or ask_<slot>_dtmf at the keypad rung where the slot takes keys), a step on its ladder, and a second no goes to a person. The right answer said with the no ("no, it's ...") is taken.

confirmValues.description: Options (their keys) read back for a yes as soon as one is chosen, as with `confirm: always` (confirm_<slot>, given the option's display as {<slot>}); any other option follows `confirm`. For the answer that ends the call or turns a caller away ("rent", not "own"). Default: none.

readBack.description: With `confirm: by-confidence`, what a chosen option asks for: "implicit" (always acknowledged; the default), "below-fill" (only when the model is less sure of it than SLOT_CHOICE_FILL), "none" (never, unless the caller hedged).

disambiguate.description: "margin": the slot reads the model's probability for every label, not only its pick, and when a second option is within SLOT_CHOICE_MARGIN of the top one (or, while the caller hedges, reaches SLOT_CHOICE_CONFIRM) it asks which of the two (disambiguate_<slot>, given {a} and {b}). The top option must then reach SLOT_CHOICE_CONFIRM before anything else is read. Default: off.

hedge.description: A second question, a yes-or-no: is the caller unsure which option they mean? A hedged option is read back however sure the model is (with `confirm: by-confidence`); with `disambiguate`, a hedged rival that reaches SLOT_CHOICE_CONFIRM is asked about. Its id is `ids.hedge` (default: <slot>Hedge).

threshold.description: The threshold the model's yes must reach for the caller to count as unsure: an engine threshold, or one of the app's own (app.yaml thresholds), read from the turn by name.

byName.description: While the caller hedges, ask which of two when their words name another option as a whole word (its key, underscores as spaces, case aside), though the model put its weight on one.

text.description: Text to say to the model in place of a default, word for word, by part: instructions, true, false.

instructions.description: The question that asks whether the caller is unsure which option they mean.

true.description: What a yes means: the caller hedges.

false.description: What a no means: the caller is sure, or names nothing.

help.description: A third question, asked on every turn: what does the caller say without naming an option ("I do not know the name")? When no option is chosen and the model's top label reaches `threshold` and has a prompt, the slot asks for help with that line (a help outcome) instead of being absent. Its id is `ids.help` (default: <slot>Help).

threshold.description: The threshold the model's top label must reach to lead to its line.

means.description: What the model is told this label is: the text of its criterion, sent exactly as written.

prompt.description: The line said when the model chooses this label (a help outcome). None: the label asks for no help (the slot is absent).

labels.description: The labels of the help question, in order, as `label: { means, prompt? }`. The first must have no prompt: it is the answer that asks for no help, which a stub model chooses when nothing is said.

text.description: Text to say to the model in place of a default, word for word, by part: instructions.

instructions.description: The question that asks what the caller says about the question without naming an option; its labels are `help.labels`.

ids.description: Question ids in place of the defaults: `ids.choice` is the question's id (default: the slot's own id), `ids.hedge` and `ids.help` those of the hedge and help questions (default: <slot>Hedge, <slot>Help), to keep the ids an existing slot used.

choice.description: The id of the question that asks which of the options the caller names.

hedge.description: The id of the question that asks whether the caller is unsure which option they mean.

help.description: The id of the question that asks what the caller says about the question without naming an option.

oneOf.description: One of a fixed list of options: a delivery speed, a branch, a colour.

range.description: Which days the slot takes. "future": today or a day to come (an appointment, a delivery); "tomorrow" and "Monday" are the next ones. "past": today or a day gone, up to two years back (when something happened); "yesterday" and "Monday" are the last ones.

windows.description: `range: future` only. Whether the caller may name a span of days ("next week", "in December") rather than a day: the span is held as the partial { kind: window, start, end, label }, the `narrowPrompt` asks which day in it, and a bare weekday said next is looked for inside it. Adds the window question.

qualifier.description: Whether to ask if a weekday is "this" one or "next" one. Adds the qualifier question. Ahead (`range: future`), "next Tuesday" is in the next week and "this Tuesday" this week's (next week's once it is gone). Back (`range: past`), "next Tuesday" is a day to come, refused (reason future, re-asked with `futurePrompt`), and "this Tuesday" this week's (the week from Monday) when it is today or gone, else refused the same way. Without it, a weekday is the next one ahead and the last one back, whatever word comes before it.

narrowPrompt.description: With `windows`: the prompt that asks which day in a span of days (the slot's partialPromptId), given {window} ("next week", "in December"). Default: ask_<slot>_narrow.

nearFuture.description: `range: past` only. What a month and day still to come this year is when it is at most 31 days ahead ("October 22nd" said on October 17th). "refuse" (the default): this year's, a day that has not happened, so it is refused (invalid, reason future, re-asked with `futurePrompt` when the caller was asked for the day, else absent), never moved into the past; further ahead it is last year's ("December fifth" said in September). The mirror of `range: future`, where a month and day more than 31 days gone is next year's. "last-year": last year's however near, as before 2026-10-17.

futurePrompt.description: `range: past`, when a day to come can be heard (`nearFuture: refuse`, the default, or `qualifier`): the line that asks again for the day after the caller named one that has not happened ("That date hasn't happened yet. What date did it happen?"), the retry at the open rung for reason future. Default: ask_<slot>_future.

sayYear.description: Whether the display says the year. "other-year" (the default): when the day is not in this year ("Wednesday, October 22, 2025"; in Spanish "miércoles, 22 de octubre de 2025"), so a caller hears which year a read-back means; a day this year is said without it ("Thursday, September 10"). "never": never, as before 2026-10-17.

preferMonthDay.description: Whether a month and a day the model is sure of (SLOT_CHOICE_CONFIRM) win over a weekday reading of the mode: "Monday, September 28" names one day twice, and a weekday reading would land on the next or last Monday instead of the date said.

fillAt.description: How sure the model must be of the day (the least of the parts it read) for it to count. "fill": SLOT_CHOICE_FILL; a day below it is treated as not resolved (`whenUnresolved`). "confirm": SLOT_CHOICE_CONFIRM; a day below it is invalid (reason low_confidence, raw the ISO day), and `readBack` says whether one below SLOT_CHOICE_FILL is acknowledged.

whenUnsaid.description: What a turn that names no day (the mode question answers none, is below SLOT_CHOICE_CONFIRM, or is not answered at all) gives. "invalid-if-prompted": invalid (reason unresolvable, raw empty) when the caller was asked for the day, so the retry ladder moves on, else absent. "absent": always absent.

whenUnresolved.description: What a day named but not resolved (no such day, out of range, a span without `windows`, or below the `fillAt` threshold under "fill") gives. "invalid-if-prompted": invalid (reason unresolvable, raw empty) when the caller was asked for the day, else absent. "invalid": always invalid (reason unresolvable), its raw the mode the caller used (absolute, weekday, ...).

keypad.description: Whether the caller can key the day on the keypad as four digits, month then day (MMDD: 0922), or in a day-first locale (Spanish) day then month (DDMM: 2209), resolved as a spoken month and day are for the `range`. Needs an ask_<slot>_dtmf line.

The right answer said with the no ("no, it's ...") is taken.

readBack.description: With `confirm: by-confidence`, what a filled day asks for: "implicit" (always acknowledged), "below-fill" (only when the model is less sure of it than SLOT_CHOICE_FILL), "none" (never).

context.description: The sentence each default question starts with after "Read asr.text.", saying what day the caller is giving ("The caller is saying which day a parcel was due."). Default, by `range`: "The caller is saying the day something happened." (past), "The caller is saying the day they want." (future).

exclude.description: A sentence naming a date the caller may also say that is not this day ("A date of birth is not the day the parcel was due."), which the default mode, month and day questions end with. Default: none.

text.description: Text to say to the model in place of a default, word for word, by part: mode, modeNone, relative, weekday, qualifier, month, day, window.

mode.description: The question that asks how the caller refers to the day: a relative day, a weekday, a month and day, a span of days (with `windows`), or none. By default {modes} describes each choice for the slot's `range`, and the question ends with the `exclude` sentence.

modeNone.description: What the mode question's "none" choice means (its criterion), such as which dates are not this day. Default: nothing (the label alone).

relative.description: The question that asks which relative day the caller says: today, yesterday or the day before (`range: past`), or today, tomorrow or the day after (`range: future`).

weekday.description: The question that asks which day of the week the caller names.

qualifier.description: With `qualifier`: the question that asks whether a weekday is "this" one or "next" one.

month.description: The question that asks which month the caller names. By default it ends with the `exclude` sentence.

day.description: The question that asks which day of the month the caller names. By default it ends with the `exclude` sentence.

window.description: With `windows`: the question that asks which span of days the caller names.

ids.description: Question ids in place of the defaults (the slot's id followed by the part: mode, relative, weekday, qualifier, month, day, window), to keep the ids an existing slot used.

mode.description: The id of the question that asks how the caller refers to the day.

relative.description: The id of the question that asks which relative day the caller says.

weekday.description: The id of the question that asks which day of the week the caller names.

qualifier.description: The id of the question that asks whether a weekday is this one or next one.

month.description: The id of the question that asks which month the caller names.

day.description: The id of the question that asks which day of the month the caller names.

window.description: The id of the question that asks which span of days the caller names.

listen.description: Where the slot listens outside a form. "up-front": asked there, and a value kept only when the turn enters a form that has the slot (values said up front with the request). "form": asked and filled only while a form that has it is open; outside one its question is not sent. "anywhere": a value said outside a form is kept when said on a turn that opens no form, or with the request for a form that has the slot, until a form that has the slot uses it; a turn that opens a form without it keeps nothing for it. "call": as anywhere, and kept for the whole call, across forms (what app.yaml's carrySlots does). An identity factor listens as identity.yaml says, and takes none. Without it, the slot listens as its forms say (forms.yaml listenBeforeEntered): "form" when every form that lists it says false (the default for an internal form), else "up-front".

offer.description: Propose a value in place of the question. "facts": when the form would ask the slot and the app's facts have a value for it (code.facts.offers; e.g. the street the call-start lookup found for the number calling, or one a form's entry call loaded after identity), the line asks offer_<slot> as a yes or no, with the value as {<slot>} ("Is this about 22 Alder Street?"), once per slot per form. A yes fills the slot with it, confirmed, and nothing else: never who the caller is or their identity level. A no asks ask_<slot> with no attempt counted, and a value said instead fills as said. Needs code.facts.offers, and offer_<slot> in every locale. Never on an identity factor, nor beside callerNumber, nor on a slot redacted by its length (its words are never said back).

offerAt.description: Where a slot with offer: facts proposes. "slot" (the default): when its form would ask it. "greeting": at call start, on a call, after the call-start lookup, in place of the greeting's open question (greeting_offer, then offer_<slot>), when the facts have a value for it then; otherwise at the slot. One greeting proposal per call, the first such slot in slots.yaml order. A yes fills the slot, confirmed, kept for whichever form uses it, and greet_after_offer asks the open question; a yes with a request goes on to the request. A no, or a request with neither, leaves the slot to be asked in its form, not proposed again there. Needs offer: facts, and greeting_offer and greet_after_offer in every locale.

offerAnswers.description: What a slot with offer: facts takes at its proposal. "yes-no-or-value" (the default): a yes, a no, or a value of the caller's own, which fills the slot as said. "yes-no": a yes or a no only. A value said at the proposal is not taken, and with no clear yes it is a no (the slot's question is then asked); on the keypad 1 is yes and 2 is no. Use yes-no where the line asks only a yes or no question ("Are you calling about the account ending in 1234?"). Needs offer: facts.

askedOf.description: The callers the slot is asked of: principal kinds as identity.yaml names them (the subject kind, or a delegate kind such as broker), or a delegate kind and one of its roles (broker.office_admin). For any other caller the slot is not part of its forms: its question is not sent, it is not asked, and its form completes without it (a caller not yet verified is no kind listed but anonymous, which may not be listed). Use it for what only some callers need to say, such as which client a delegate is asking about. Never on an identity factor; pnpm check refuses a kind or a role identity.yaml does not have. Default: every caller.

attempts.description: How many failed answers the slot takes before onMaxAttempts, 1 to 10. Each failure before the last but one re-asks: a missed answer with ask_<slot>_retry, or ask_<slot>_retry2 at the second failure (and so on) where prompts.yaml has it; a silence with ask_<slot>_noinput2 (and so on), else ask_<slot>_noinput, else no_input then the question (ask_<slot>) again (at the keypad rung of a slot that takes no keys, on a channel with a keypad, no_input then its retry line). The last but one is the keypad rung (ask_<slot>_dtmf) where the slot takes keys and the channel has a keypad, else another re-ask; the last runs onMaxAttempts. Default: the engine's MAX_ATTEMPTS (3).

say.description: The line said (a prompt in prompts.yaml); it renders with the form's slot displays as variables, as the summary does. Required for end and anything-else; for the others, said first.

then.description: What follows the line: end (the call ends after the line; with a request queued, the call goes on to it); anything-else (the form closes uncompleted and the call carries on: the next queued request, or "anything else?"); handoff (to a person, with the handoff line handoff_<reason>); form (the form closes uncompleted and the form named by `form` is entered, as a next: is, keeping the slots both list); skip (the slot is left empty and declined, and the form goes on to its next question).

reason.description: For then: handoff, the handoff reason, whose line is handoff_<reason>. Default: max-attempts.

form.description: For then: form, the form entered: a form in forms.yaml (an internal one too).

goodbye.description: For then: end, whether the app's goodbye line follows `say`. false: the call ends on `say` alone, for a line that says goodbye itself ("... We're closed right now. Goodbye."), so the caller does not hear goodbye twice. Default true: the goodbye follows the line. Either way, with a request queued the line is said and the call goes on to it, so a line that may be followed by one keeps the goodbye out of its words (only a start route never has one).

onMaxAttempts.description: What happens when the slot runs out of attempts (a missed answer, a silence, an unanswered read-back, or a second no to its read-back). "handoff" (the default): to a person, with handoff_max_attempts. "skip": the slot is left empty and declined, and the form goes on; never on an identity factor, nor on a slot its form's summary names. Or written out, { say, then, reason, form, goodbye }: then is handoff (reason names the handoff, default max-attempts), skip, end (say required; the call ends, the goodbye after the line unless goodbye: false), anything-else (say required; the form closes uncompleted and "anything else?" is asked) or form (the form closes uncompleted and `form` is entered, keeping the slots both list); say, a prompt said first. An offer of the caller's number with onNo: skip that runs out leaves the slot empty whatever this says; with no onNo: skip, the slot's ladder goes on to it.

oneOf.description: A calendar day, ahead or back: an appointment, a delivery, the day something happened.

noun.description: What the number identifies, as a noun without "number" ("account", "library card", "parcel tracking"). The default questions say "a <noun> number". Needed unless text gives every question in its own words.

article.description: The word before the noun in the default questions. Default: "an" when the noun starts with a vowel, otherwise "a".

length.description: How many digits the number has. Gives the default mask (exactly this many digits) and the length of the keypad rung. Needed unless mask is given.

mask.description: A regular expression (its source, no slashes) the whole of the digits must match: it is anchored at both ends, so "5\d{7}" and "^5\d{7}$" both mean eight digits starting with 5. With `length` too, the digits must also be that many. Default: exactly `length` digits. A number that fails it is "invalid" with the reason "mask" (with only `length`, the reason is "length"). A group that repeats a repeat, such as (\d+)+, is refused.

keypad.description: Whether the caller can key the number on the keypad, `length` digits at a time. Needs `length`, and an ask_<slot>_dtmf line.

group.description: How the number is said back, in groups of these sizes ([4, 4]: "5550 7788"). The last group takes any digits left over. Default: all digits together.

confirm.description: "summary": a spoken number is neither acknowledged nor read back on its own; the form's final confirm covers it. "by-confidence": it is acknowledged (ack_<slot>) when `readBack` says so. "always": a spoken number is read back for a yes as soon as it is heard (confirm_<slot>, given its display as {<slot>}), before the form goes on; a no empties the slot and asks it again (ack_declined, then ask_<slot>, or ask_<slot>_dtmf at the keypad rung where the slot takes keys), a step on its ladder, and a second no goes to a person. The right answer said with the no ("no, it's ...") is taken.

readBack.description: What a filled number asks for: "implicit" (always), "below-fill" (only when the model is less sure of the span than SLOT_CHOICE_FILL), "none" (never). With `confirm: by-confidence`, "implicit" is what makes ack_<slot> be said.

minConfidence.description: A floor on how sure the model must be of the span: below this threshold the number is "invalid" (reason "low_confidence"). "none": no floor.

lengthRetryPromptId.description: The prompt that re-asks, in place of the generic ask_<slot>_retry, when what the caller said is not a number of the right shape ("A card number has eight digits.").

redact.description: How the value is masked wherever it leaves the turn (the trace, the console, the audit, a tool call's param of the same name): "last4" ("...0417"; a number of four digits or fewer, whose last four would be all of it, as "••••"), "length" (only how many digits, "<4 chars>", its display too and on the live console, its keys masked as they are keyed, and a transfer handed only its length: for a short secret such as a PIN) or "none".

callerNumber.description: Offer the number the caller is calling from: when the form would ask this slot and the call has a number that fits it (its `countryCode`, `length` and `mask`), the line asks offer_<slot> ("Is the number you're calling from, ending in {last4}, the best one to reach you?") in place of ask_<slot>, and a yes fills the slot with that number. A no asks ask_<slot>, with no attempt counted, and a number said instead fills as said. The line may say the whole number too, {callerNumber}. A chat, or a call with no number (a withheld placeholder, or a withheld number the app ignores: app.yaml's callerNumber.withheld), is asked ask_<slot> as always. Never on an identity factor: a caller ID can be forged.

countryCode.description: The country calling code the carrier writes before the number ("1" for +1). A number in international form (+15555550142, as carriers send it) must begin with it, and it is taken off; one from any other country is no number for the slot. A number with no + has it taken off when what is left has the slot's `length`.

onNo.description: What a no to the offer does: "ask" (default) asks ask_<slot>, with no attempt counted; "skip" leaves the slot empty and the form goes on (an offer to text, say, where a no means no text). The end of the offer's retry ladder (no answer) does the same. A number said with the no fills the slot as said either way.

ifNone.description: What a call with no number to offer does (a chat, a withheld placeholder or a withheld number the app ignores, one that does not fit, or one the app's callerOffer hook refuses): "ask" (default) asks ask_<slot> as always; "skip" leaves the slot empty and the form goes on.

answers.description: What the offer takes: "yes-no-or-value" (default), a yes, a no, or a number of the caller's own, said or keyed, which fills the slot as said; "yes-no", a yes or a no only: a number said at the offer is not taken, and with no clear yes it is a no (onNo then says what follows), and on the keypad 1 is yes and 2 is no. Use yes-no where the line asks only a yes or no question.

handoff.description: What a transfer to a person hands over: its "last4", only whether the caller was "verified", or its "display" in full. app.yaml's handoff.data then says whether it goes, and how: by default an identity factor is left out and a redacted value masked.

sayAs.description: How the phone's voice says the value back, wherever a line says it (a read-back, a summary, the last four of the caller's number at its offer): "digits" (default), one digit at a time ("0 1 4 2"; in its `group`s with a short pause between them, "5 5 5 0, 7 7 8 8"), as a caller reads a number out; "number", as the voice reads it ("one hundred forty-two"), for a value that is a quantity rather than an identifier. Only what is sent to the voice is rewritten, after voice.spokenDigits: the session, the trace, the console and a chat keep the digits as written.

waitForRestMs.description: On the phone, how long to wait for the rest of a number the caller began, in milliseconds: when the slot was just asked and heard fewer digits than `length` (or a number the model heard trail off), and the turn would only ask again, the re-ask is held this long; if the caller goes on in that time it is never said, and their next words are joined to the first ("five", a pause, "five five two zero four one seven" is 55520417). A caller who said all they meant to hears the re-ask this much later. 0 asks again at once. Not on a chat, where a message comes whole. Default: 1500, a reader's pause to look at the number again; 0 to 5000.

span.description: The threshold the model's probability for the name span must reach: an engine threshold, or one of the app's own (app.yaml thresholds), read from the turn by name. Default: NAME_BARE_SPAN (0.7).

say.description: The line said (a prompt in prompts.yaml); it renders with the form's slot displays as variables, as the summary does. Required for end and anything-else; for the others, said first.

then.description: What follows the line: end (the call ends after the line; with a request queued, the call goes on to it); anything-else (the form closes uncompleted and the call carries on: the next queued request, or "anything else?"); handoff (to a person, with the handoff line handoff_<reason>); form (the form closes uncompleted and the form named by `form` is entered, as a next: is, keeping the slots both list); skip (the slot is left empty and declined, and the form goes on to its next question).

reason.description: For then: handoff, the handoff reason, whose line is handoff_<reason>. Default: max-attempts.

form.description: For then: form, the form entered: a form in forms.yaml (an internal one too).

goodbye.description: For then: end, whether the app's goodbye line follows `say`. false: the call ends on `say` alone, for a line that says goodbye itself ("... We're closed right now. Goodbye."), so the caller does not hear goodbye twice. Default true: the goodbye follows the line. Either way, with a request queued the line is said and the call goes on to it, so a line that may be followed by one keeps the goodbye out of its words (only a start route never has one).

onMaxAttempts.description: What happens when the slot runs out of attempts (a missed answer, a silence, an unanswered read-back, or a second no to its read-back). oneOf.description: The caller's own name, first and last as they say it: "Anna Petrov", "Sam".

from.description: The list of records to choose among, by name: the app gives its lists by name from facts.forSlots ({ sources: { <name>: [...] } }), so two record slots can each read their own. Default: the app's one list (facts.forSlots records).

key.description: The record field whose value the slot takes (a string or a number), and which the keypad and a spoken number give.

keyPattern.description: A regular expression (its source, no slashes) the whole key must match, such as "\d{4}" for four digits. A record whose key does not match is not offered, and a label or keys that do not match are no value. labelPrefix.description: What each label the model chooses starts with, before the key ("parcel_" gives parcel_4711). It keeps a key from being taken for the question's own "none".

label.description: The criterion the model is given for each record. A template: {field} is the record's field of that name, {key} the record's key, and {field|day} formats an ISO date as a day ("Friday, September 18"). Nothing else is evaluated.

display.description: What the slot's value is said as (its display: the read-back, a line that names it, the console): a template over the record's fields, as `label` is ("{label}" for a time a schedule labels "Saturday, October 24 at 10:30 AM"). spoken.description: Numbers of `digits` digits the caller says (spoken or written) are offered too, after the records, even when no record has them, so a caller can name one that is not on their list. Default: off, only the records are offered.

digits.description: How many digits a number the caller says has.

label.default: Number {key}, as the caller said it
label.description: The criterion the model is given for a number the caller says; {key} is the number. A template: {field} is the record's field of that name, {key} the record's key, and {field|day} formats an ISO date as a day ("Friday, September 18"). Nothing else is evaluated.

skipYearAfterMonth.description: Whether a spoken year right after a month name ("March twenty twenty five") is a date rather than a number.

missReason.description: The reason of the invalid outcome when the slot was asked for and the caller chose nothing (or the model was not sure enough). Not asked for, that is absent.

keypad.description: How many keys the caller keys the key with, after spoken answers missed; the keys are the value when they match keyPattern. Needs an ask_<slot>_dtmf line. Default: no keypad.

disambiguate.description: Whether two records the model cannot tell apart (the top two within SLOT_CHOICE_MARGIN) make the slot ask which one (disambiguate_<slot>, with {a} and {b}).

fillAt.description: The threshold the model's probability for the record must reach for the slot to fill. Below SLOT_CHOICE_CONFIRM nothing was chosen.

confirm.description: "summary" (the default): a record is neither acknowledged nor read back on its own; the form's final confirm covers it. text.description: Text to say to the model in place of a default, word for word, by part: instructions, none.

instructions.description: The question that asks which record the caller means, sent to the model in place of the default.

none.description: What the question's "none" label means: the caller names no record.

ids.description: Question ids in place of the default: `ids.choice` is the question's id (default: the slot's id followed by "Choice"), to keep the id an existing slot used.

choice.description: The id of the question that asks which record the caller means.

listen.description: Where the slot listens outside a form. "up-front": asked there, and a value kept only when the turn enters a form that has the slot (values said up front with the request). "form": asked and filled only while a form that has it is open; outside one its question is not sent. "anywhere": a value said outside a form is kept when said on a turn that opens no form, or with the request for a form that has the slot, until a form that has the slot uses it; a turn that opens a form without it keeps nothing for it. "call": as anywhere, and kept for the whole call, across forms (what app.yaml's carrySlots does). An identity factor listens as identity.yaml says, and takes none. Without it, the slot listens as its forms say (forms.yaml listenBeforeEntered): "form" when every form that lists it says false (the default for an internal form), else "up-front".

offer.description: Propose a value in place of the question. offerAt.description: Where a slot with offer: facts proposes. "slot" (the default): when its form would ask it. oneOf.description: A code of letters and digits of a set length: a booking code, an order reference.

what.description: What the caller gives, as a noun phrase the default question names ("a description of the problem"). Needed unless text.given gives the question in its own words.

instructions.description: More guidance for the model, added after the default question ("Count it even when it comes with a request.").

maxLength.description: The most characters of the caller's words the value keeps; the rest is cut off.

say.description: The display: what a line, the console and the model's turn state show in place of the words ("your note"). null: the words themselves.

keep.description: When a value is on file: "first-unless-prompted" replaces it only when the slot was just asked for; "first" never does. A correction at the summary replaces it either way. A yes to the summary keeps it, unless the yes names the slot to change or (without `pick`) gives new or changed words for it (the `changed` question, at SUMMARY_WORDS_CHANGED or more), when the turn's words are added after them, exactly as said (read again where the action's confirmed rule holds the write to what the summary said).

redact.description: "length": the words leave the turn (the trace, a tool call's param) as their length only, and the display is kept. "none": as they are. "length-summarized": for words a model summarizes in a framed read-back (a span worded from them; never a line generated whole from them): kept in the session so the app's lines say them and a tool is sent them, sent whole to the render model only for that span, and masked by their length in every record (the trace, the frame log, the console, the audit, a handoff, the display too); in such an app every caller's words are kept by their length in those records, and no other line is sent them. The one named exception to "a model is never sent a value the records hide whole"; the policy card lists it. Refused on an identity factor and on a slot no framed span summarizes (use length there).

what.description: What the value is, as a noun phrase the pick question names ("the street address").

words.description: The joining words and prepositions by language tag ("fr", or "fr-CA" for one region, whose missing list is the language's), for a language with no built-in list or to replace one. Built in: English ("and", "but", "so", "because"; "at", "on", "in", "near", "by", "for"), also read with no locale, and Spanish ("y", "e", "pero", "porque", "así que"; "en", "cerca de", "junto a"). A language with neither splits at punctuation only.

joiners.description: Words or phrases that join two clauses, where the words are split ("et", "parce que"). Replaces the built-in list of the language.

prepositions.description: Words or phrases after which a clause's tail is offered too ("au", "près de"). Replaces the built-in list of the language.

additionalProperties.description: The words of one language: either list left out is the built-in one.

pick.description: Pick the value out of the words. Code splits the caller's words into candidate parts (clauses, split at punctuation and at joining words, and each clause's tail after a preposition; then two clauses side by side joined as said, and that join's tails; at most 8 of these; then the tails from each word of a clause or a join to its end, of 2 words or more, the shortest kept, so a value after any lead-in can be chosen; each verbatim, at most 16 in all), and a second question (`ids.pick`, default `<slot>Pick`) asks which of them is `pick.what`, by letter, or none of these. The value is the part chosen, as said; none, a choice below SLOT_DETECT, or words that make one candidate keep the whole words. Default: off, the value is the whole words and only the one question is asked.

numbers.description: How the value writes the numbers the caller says in words. "words": as said. "digits": code writes each run of number words as digits ("seventy six twenty five oak hollow lane" is "7625 oak hollow lane", "one zero two four six" is "10246", "one oh two" is "102"); ordinals stay words ("fifth avenue", "twenty third street"), and so do digits already said. The value (a tool's param, the gate, the audit, the console) is written; with say: null the display, which a line reads back, stays the words as said, since text-to-speech reads "7625" as a quantity. With pick, the part picked is written. Only in a language with rules: English, also read with no locale; another keeps the words as said.

case.description: How the value writes the case of the words. "as-said": as the recognizer or the caller wrote them. "title": words written with no capital at all (a recognizer that writes none) have each word capitalized, but for minor words after the first ("7625 oak hollow lane" is "7625 Oak Hollow Lane"); words with any capital stay as they are. The value only: with say: null the display stays the words as said. Only in a language with rules: English, also read with no locale.

others.description: What the other slots do on a turn that gives this slot its words while it is the slot just asked for: the app decides, by its business. "quiet": the turn is this slot's content, and no other slot fills or changes from it, so a word in a message ("could someone send it again") never replaces a value already given (who the message is for). "listen": every slot listens on that turn too, so a caller who names another value in the same breath as the words gives it ("14 Birch Lane, and there's a line down"). { listen: [<slot>, ...] }: quiet, but for the slots listed, which still fill or change from that turn (an urgency slot read from the content of a message). Default: "quiet" for a slot that takes the whole answer as its content (no `pick`), "listen" for one that picks part of a longer answer (`pick`). It applies only on a turn that gives this slot its words: a turn where the caller gives no text, or where another slot was asked, fills every slot. Whether that turn is read for requests (an urgent request, asking for a person, a question) is `commands`; either way the injection screen reads it, the form a turn switches to hears it whole, and a correction at a read-back or the summary changes any slot.

listen.description: The slots that still fill or change from the turn that gives this slot its words: each a slot of a form that holds this one (an urgency read from the content of a message). pnpm check refuses any other.

commands.description: Whether the turn that answers this slot's question is read for requests: the app decides, by its business. "ignore": the turn is the slot's words, whole (when the line listens for a message, that is the message): the slot's own question sets no bar, so whatever is said is the value, and nothing in it is acted on as a request: no intent, priority switch, repeat, request for a person, menu number or frustration, and words that sound like an aside are taken too. Still as on any turn: the injection screen, silence, words the model cannot make out (asked again), a partial held for the rest, and an unfinished answer joined to what the caller goes on with; the read-back follows as ever, so the caller hears the words and can say no. "listen": the turn is read as any other: every request is acted on, and the words fill the slot only where its question reads them as given (SLOT_DETECT). { listen: [<intent>, ...] }: as "ignore", but the intents listed are acted on when the turn makes one (asking for a person is `agent`, which takes in the wantsHuman gate; a repeat is `repeat_prompt`), and every other turn is the slot's words. Default: "ignore" for a slot that takes the whole answer as its content (no `pick`), "listen" for one that picks part of a longer answer (`pick`). It applies only where this slot was the one just asked for, with no read-back or offer pending, and the turn has words, and never to an identity factor: a turn at another question, answering a read-back, or proving who the caller is, is read as ever.
